summary.intent: Create Phase 60 planning artifacts (PLAN.md files) for an IPNS verification cross-layer closeout covering three work streams: desktop verified-resolve routing, API hot-path verify caching, and first-publish strict-equality cutover — using the GSD plan-phase workflow with two recon passes to establish safe scope before planning.
summary.outcome: 8 plans in 4 waves committed on `feat/ipns-verification-cross-layer-closeout-desktop-and-api` (ec3f1ab62) with all 12 verification dimensions passing. Scope expanded significantly from the original todos: 9 embed-0 producer sites (up from 3), 14 degraded-acceptance branches across 4 layers, and a verified-resolve wrapper relocation to crates/api-client.

repo: The IPNS embedded sequence lives inside the signed CBOR blob (covered by the V2 signature), not the plaintext protobuf field-5 copy — changing it requires re-signing with the Ed25519 private key; the API server has no signing primitive at all.

The API hard-codes first-publish DB sequence_number to '1' regardless of whether the client embedded 0 or 1 (ipns.service.ts:356-362), and a prior backfill migration already normalized all '0' rows to '1' — so `sequence_number = 0` cannot be used to identify the embedded-0 population.

TEE republish is NOT idempotent: it increments sequence by 1n and persists the new signed record (republish.ts:79), so enrolled embedded-0 FUSE folders self-migrate to strict-equality-compatible state within one 6-hour cycle — no bespoke migration tooling needed for enrolled rows.

TEE republish path bypasses verifyIpnsRecordSignature entirely (calls publishSignedRecord + syncFolderIpnsSequence directly), so the D-11 cache can only short-circuit exact-bytes client re-submission — never untrusted or DHT records.
The verified-resolve wrapper must be created in crates/api-client, not cipherbox-fuse, because cipherbox-sdk does not depend on cipherbox-fuse.

There are 9 embed-0 first-publish producers (not 3 as the original todo stated): FUSE mkdir, FUSE windows write_ops, FUSE metadata bin, web useAuth vault-key, web useAuth root-folder, web vault-settings, SDK vault-key, desktop vault.rs vault-key, desktop vault.rs root-folder.
The two web useAuth.ts sites (vault-key + root-folder) fire on every new vault creation — they are the highest-impact embed-0 sites and must be fixed before any strict-equality flip.
crates/sdk/src/registry.rs and sync.rs call raw resolve_ipns with zero verification (accepts a tampered CID), strictly worse than the Legacy path — this was unmentioned in the original todos.

FUSE crash-recovery replay path was already unified to embed 1 in Phase 59 (crates/fuse/src/replay.rs:628); the V1-only acceptance path is structurally impossible at resolve since IpnsResolveResponse carries only signature_v2.

No production instance exists yet; staging self-bootstraps strict-compliant records on next login after a wipe — eliminates the entire embedded-0 live-migration problem and justifies the clean rip-out approach over a gated migration.

workflow: Running two independent recon workflows before planning (one on migration mechanics, one on blast radius) was essential — the first corrected a false claim about TEE idempotency, the second expanded producer count from 3 to 9 and found unverified SDK bypasses the todos never mentioned.
The GSD commit_failed signal from the helper is a known false negative — always verify via git log rather than treating it as a real failure.
PATTERNS.md is not auto-committed by the plan-phase workflow and requires a manual commit step after the pattern-mapper agent completes.

The decision-coverage gate parser does not recognize the D-NN bullet format used in CONTEXT.md and silently skips — the plan-checker's substantive review is the real gate; the CLI gate is unreliable for non-standard formats.

Writing CONTEXT.md with all locked decisions before spawning the planner is the key contract artifact — it lets the planner work from a single authoritative source rather than re-deriving from transcript.

When multiple independent recon workflows are needed, their findings can contradict each other — always resolve contradictions by reading source directly rather than trusting the summary of either agent.

friction: Initial scope (from the todo) named 3 embed-0 producer sites; two recon workflows were required to establish the correct count of 9 — planning would have produced dangerously incomplete plans without this.

One recon subagent gave a flat-out wrong claim that TEE republish is idempotent; it required a third agent to read source directly and resolve the contradiction before the migration mechanics answer could be trusted.
The GSD commit_failed false negative from the helper creates uncertainty after every commit — requires a manual `git log` check to confirm success.
PATTERNS.md is silently dropped by the plan-phase workflow — not auto-committed, not mentioned as a gap in the workflow docs; discovered only when auditing what was and wasn't staged.
The decision-coverage gate CLI parser doesn't handle the D-NN bullet format in CONTEXT.md and exits silently rather than erroring — gives false confidence that coverage was checked.

Staging wipe + smoke test is a blocking human action in Wave 4 (Plan 60-08) — cannot be automated.

Resolve-side expiry check (no EOL validation on resolve in either verifier) is included in scope but represents net-new hardening beyond what the original todos captured — scope increase to monitor during execution.
The SDK verified-resolve wrapper design (D-08) requires creating a new primitive in crates/api-client — the exact API surface is TBD for the executor of Plan 60-01.
D-11 hot-path caching requires a benchmark-before-mechanism gate (Plan 60-06 measures first) — if benchmarks show negligible cost, the caching design may be dropped.
